chapter: The Vitaphone film and studio work
title: Playing at the homes of film stars
summary: The studio work led to parties for Basil Rathbone, Charlie Chaplin and Marion Davies, who wanted jazz because white musicians did not play it.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Jazz musicians on film and studio scoring

blocks.x: And as a result of playing in the studios like this, you probably got more jobs playing for what? Parties and things?
Yeah. Used to...I played for nearly all the big stars at their homes and things--Basil Rathbone, Charlie Chaplin, and what was the woman that was...went with Randolph Hearst? Marian Davis, was it?
Yeah, we played at her home down at the beach. Oh, around like that, you know. See the white boys those days wasn't playing jazz, you know.
And all these people wanted to hear jazz?
Yeah, it was new, so they call us.
